title: Manual Breathing Devices & Pharyngeal Airways Quiz

questions.text: A manual breathing device is used primarily to:

answers.text: Provide positive pressure ventilation to patients not breathing adequately

questions.text: When should supplemental oxygen be attached to the BVM?

answers.text: As soon as appropriate and when enough resources are available
Only after the patient is extubated
Only when a flow-inflating bag is unavailable

questions.text: Which situation is an indication for manual ventilation?

answers.text: Spontaneous breathing is absent or insufficient for gas exchange
The patient has normal spontaneous ventilation and no distress
The patient needs a routine neurologic history
The patient needs a daily tracheal speaking valve cleaning

questions.text: Why can positive pressure ventilation decrease cardiac output?

answers.text: It increases intrathoracic pressure and decreases venous return
It increases urine output above 3 L/day
It removes the need for oxygenation

questions.text: Gastric insufflation during manual ventilation increases the risk for:
Which advantage belongs to a self-inflating manual resuscitation bag?

answers.text: It does not need a gas source to operate
It always requires a sealed gas source to inflate
It is only used for chest tube drainage
It cannot be used during CPR

questions.text: At 15 L/min, a self-inflating manual resuscitation bag can deliver approximately:
A flow-inflating resuscitation bag is mainly used:

answers.text: In the operating room by anesthesia and with neonates
Only for adult chest tube drainage
Only for Glasgow Coma Scale scoring

questions.text: Peak inspiratory pressure with a flow-inflating bag is controlled by flow, valve adjustment, and:

answers.text: How hard the bag is squeezed

questions.text: Which disadvantage belongs to a flow-inflating bag?

answers.text: It inflates only when the gas source is on and the opening is sealed
It cannot let the user feel lung compliance

questions.text: A PEEP valve is especially important during manual ventilation when:

answers.text: The ventilator PEEP setting is high, especially over 5 cm H2O
The patient has no need for oxygen
The patient is being scored with APACHE II
The chest tube water seal is bubbling

questions.text: The head-tilt/chin-lift technique opens the airway by:

answers.text: Pressing the forehead down while lifting the bony underside of the chin
Lowering the head of bed and raising the feet
Placing a chest tube in the fifth intercostal space

questions.text: Which maneuver is preferred when head, neck, or spinal injury is suspected?
The source gives the adult manual ventilation rate as:
During adult BVM ventilation, the bag is depressed about halfway to deliver:
In two-person BVM technique, Provider 1 primarily:

answers.text: Maintains the mask seal and open airway with both hands

questions.text: An oropharyngeal airway is designed to:

answers.text: Prevent the tongue from obstructing the hypopharynx
Drain blood from the pleural space
Seal the esophagus with a distal cuff

questions.text: Which patient is an OPA contraindicated for?

answers.text: An unconscious patient with tongue obstruction
An intubated patient needing a bite block
A patient with no gag reflex

questions.text: Correct OPA sizing measures from the corner of the mouth to the:
Which condition is an absolute contraindication for NPA insertion?

answers.text: Need for an airway tolerated by a conscious patient
